about: Every user-facing feature, the promise it makes, what it depends on, and the end-to-end check that proves the promise in the built app. Run: npm run verify:features (add --tier full for checks that download language models).

tiers.core: Runs offline against the built app.
tiers.network: Needs the internet (news feeds, Wikipedia, Wikidata, web pages, the beacon registry).
tiers.full: Also downloads on-device language models (about 70–80 MB each).

nodes.title: Typecheck, unit tests and production build
nodes.promise: The app is built from code that typechecks and passes every unit test.

nodes.title: App starts
nodes.promise: Intoponet opens to the globe with Private, Bookmarks, The Olds, Knowledge, My map and Settings in the header.

nodes.title: Settings and Privacy
nodes.promise: Settings covers language, automatic translation, beacons, credits and privacy; Privacy covers private browsing, footprints, sites to leave out, pins and backups.

nodes.title: Accessible and keyboard friendly
nodes.promise: No WCAG 2.2 AA violations (axe); every header panel opens with Enter, closes with Escape and returns focus to its button.

nodes.title: Modern tabs
nodes.promise: Tabs show a spinner while loading and a speaker that mutes a playing tab; they reorder by drag or keyboard, pin first as icons (kept for next launch), and stay accessible.

nodes.title: Encrypted private library, pins and beacon consent
nodes.promise: Saved pages live only in the encrypted library (old plain copies migrate without loss); pins can be hidden; publishing a pin as a beacon needs explicit agreement.

nodes.title: Collections explained and split; tags
nodes.promise: A collection explains what it holds (sites, topics, places) and can be split by site; pins carry several tags.

nodes.title: Fly to a place
nodes.promise: Typing a place (even "Charlottetown PEI" or "Fredericto") and pressing Enter spins the globe there, closes any open page and marks the exact spot.

nodes.title: Globe stays where you put it
nodes.promise: Zooming after moving the globe keeps the place in view; it never swings back.

nodes.title: Every country named and clickable
nodes.promise: Country names fade in by zoom without overlapping; the country you spin or zoom to is always named, tiny ones included (Vatican, Nauru, Tuvalu); clicking any country, with or without news, opens it.

nodes.title: Live public globe
nodes.promise: The globe shows live public signals (local news, reading, hazards) with World, Peaks, Rising and Fading highlights.

nodes.title: Sources carousel
nodes.promise: A world story with several sources opens a carousel of every outlet's headline to flip through; choosing one grows its card into the browser with that article open.

nodes.title: Stories covered across the world
nodes.promise: The World tab lists stories covered by outlets in many countries, and the whole list can be scrolled.

nodes.title: A country's news and bigger picture
nodes.promise: Opening a country shows key facts, genuinely recent history and its local headlines, without clipping.

nodes.title: The history behind a headline
nodes.promise: A headline opens the right topic with a dated, ordered chronology quoted from Wikipedia and relevant topics from the right country; broad matches give way to the actual event; no junk for unmatched headlines.

nodes.title: A country's history
nodes.promise: A country's history has key facts, chapters and events from the last ten years.

nodes.title: Competing interpretations
nodes.promise: Where Wikipedia attributes competing views, The Olds shows them side by side with who holds each.

nodes.title: The Olds panel from a headline
nodes.promise: A headline's history button opens The Olds with Story and Timeline views, no clipped timeline cards, and Escape closes it.

nodes.title: An outlet's earlier coverage
nodes.promise: From a supported outlet's headline, The Olds shows that outlet's earlier headlines on the story, newest first under the current one, credits the Wayback Machine, and goes further back without losing or reordering headlines.

nodes.title: Browse the web
nodes.promise: Pages open in tabs with a named toolbar (Translate, Capture, Pin, Absorb, Bookmarks), and closing tabs never crashes the app.

nodes.title: Address bar suggestions
nodes.promise: Typing the start of a visited site's host completes it inline (Backspace removes the completion) and offers that page first, from history or as "Switch to tab"; Enter lands on it without a duplicate tab, ⌘↵ opens it in a background tab, and a typed place name still flies the globe.

nodes.title: Ad and tracker protection
nodes.promise: Ads and trackers are blocked and the protection bar under the toolbar shows what was blocked.

nodes.title: Site permissions and sign-in popups
nodes.promise: Sites ask for camera, microphone or location in a bar you answer; sign-in popups keep working; new-tab links open as tabs.

nodes.title: Links to other apps
nodes.promise: A mailto:, tel: or zoommtg: link asks "Open <app>?" (Open / Cancel, Always allow per site) and never navigates the tab; files and scripts are never handed to other apps.

nodes.title: Error page with Retry
nodes.promise: A page that cannot load shows a clear error page in the tab (offline, can't find, too slow, not secure with certificate details) with Retry and Back; the address stays in the toolbar.

nodes.title: PDFs open in the tab
nodes.promise: PDF links open in Chromium's viewer in the tab; PDFs sent as attachments still download.

nodes.title: Light and dark pages
nodes.promise: Pages follow the Mac's light or dark appearance by default, or Light/Dark chosen in Settings, which also shows the default-browser status.

nodes.title: Private browsing
nodes.promise: Private tabs are marked, leave no footprints, and close with their session when private browsing ends.

nodes.title: Saved passwords
nodes.promise: After you sign in, Intoponet offers to save the password, keeps it sealed on this Mac, fills it next time (or asks which account), lists it in Settings, and never saves or fills in a private tab.

nodes.title: Sites to leave out
nodes.promise: Sites you leave out are never absorbed and leave no recent pages.

nodes.title: Downloads and History
nodes.promise: A download shows its progress in the toolbar’s Downloads list until it is done, lands on disk with the macOS quarantine flag, and can be opened or shown in Finder; pages visited in normal tabs appear in History (never private ones), can be searched and deleted.

nodes.title: Screenshots into folders
nodes.promise: A screenshot of the page is saved, and you can make a new folder while saving.

nodes.title: Save page as PDF
nodes.promise: One click saves the page as a tagged PDF in Downloads, formatted for reading with its source on page one and page numbers, with ads, hidden text and overlays left out, lazy images loaded, an outline of its headings, a Finder "Where from", and, when a bookmark group is chosen, a bookmark in that group linked to the PDF. Pages that are not articles are saved as seen, still without ads.

nodes.title: Paywall detection
nodes.promise: Paywalled outlets are recognised so free coverage of the same story can be offered (never circumvented).

nodes.title: Absorb, search and claims
nodes.promise: Absorbing a page (or just a selection) keeps it on this Mac; search returns the cited paragraph; claims are listed without false disputes.

nodes.title: Beacon registry on Neon
nodes.promise: The app reaches the live beacon registry, which is healthy and refuses unsigned requests.

nodes.title: Automatic page translation
nodes.promise: With automatic translation on, a Russian page is detected and translated into your language on this Mac.

nodes.title: Languages without a model
nodes.promise: Faroese headlines translate roughly through Icelandic and say so.

nodes.title: Story mountains and their strands
nodes.promise: With local news on, the tallest story raises the highest summit; the highest-peak control flies to it and pins its coverage, and Escape closes it.

nodes.title: Copy the page address from the keyboard
nodes.promise: ⌘⇧C copies the open page's address, with known tracking parameters removed, in panel and full-width views (private tabs included) and a short notice says it was copied; a page that uses ⌘⇧C itself is not broken while a text field has focus.

nodes.title: Pinned tabs keep their home
nodes.promise: A pinned tab remembers the address it was pinned at; after wandering off it shows a way back home; closing a pinned tab unloads it but keeps it in place, and it reopens at home on the next click or launch.

nodes.title: Background tabs sleep
nodes.promise: Tabs left in the background longer than the chosen time are unloaded to save memory and wake where they were (scroll and back/forward kept); tabs playing sound, sharing camera or microphone, or holding typed form text never sleep.

nodes.title: Switch tabs in the order you used them
nodes.promise: With the setting on, ⌃Tab steps through tabs most-recently-used first, holding ⌃ shows a switcher with each tab's icon and title, and releasing lands on the chosen tab; tab search in the address bar and command menu lists open tabs in the same recent order.

nodes.title: Vertical tabs in every view
nodes.promise: With vertical tabs on, the tab sidebar stays in both panel and full-width views, shows Pinned and Open sections, collapses to icons or hides fully (⌘⇧S) and slides back in when the pointer rests at the window's edge, keeps its width and state for the next launch, and every tab in it is reachable by keyboard and VoiceOver.

nodes.title: Bring your browser with you
nodes.promise: Import finds Chromium-based browsers on this Mac, previews what it will bring (bookmarks and folders as collections, pinned tabs, open tabs, optionally history and, only after the Mac asks for keychain permission, passwords) and imports only what was ticked; nothing is uploaded, and running it twice adds no duplicates.

nodes.title: The guided tour shows every feature
nodes.promise: Take the tour from Settings and every step lights up the part of the app it describes, from story mountains and their strands to the tab sidebar, PDF export and Knowledge, then puts everything back as it was.

nodes.title: Tabs tidy themselves away
nodes.promise: Unpinned tabs not looked at for the chosen time (Off, 12 hours, a day, a week, a month) close into Archived tabs, which can be searched and reopened with their back/forward list; pinned, playing, sharing and form-holding tabs are never archived, private tabs never reach the archive, and the sidebar says how many tabs were tidied.

nodes.title: Commands from the address bar
nodes.promise: ⌘K (or typing > in the address bar) lists browser actions, settings toggles, open, archived and pinned tabs, bookmarks and places, ranked as you type on this Mac; Enter runs the action (copy address, save as PDF, translate, toggle protection, switch workspace, fly to a place, open The Olds), and nothing typed leaves the device.

nodes.title: Folders in the tab sidebar
nodes.promise: Tabs can be dragged (or moved from the keyboard) into named folders that collapse, nest inside one another, keep their order for the next launch, and can be saved as a private collection or opened from one.

nodes.title: No blank boxes where ads were
nodes.promise: With protection on, the space a page kept for a blocked ad (its frame, picture or an empty slot labelled Advertisement) is hidden, while anything holding the page's own text stays; with protection paused for the site, the page is left as it is.

nodes.title: Preview a link without leaving the page
nodes.promise: ⇧-clicking a link (or choosing Preview Link) opens it in a floating card over the page, with ad and tracker protection and the same private or normal session; Escape or a click outside closes it, and Open as Tab moves the same page, with its history, into a tab; headlines on the globe and in the World list can be previewed the same way.

nodes.title: Workspaces
nodes.promise: Each workspace has its own name, icon, accent colour, pinned tabs, folders and open tabs, while a short favourites row can be shared by all of them; switching (⌃1–9, a two-finger swipe on the sidebar, or the command menu) swaps the sidebar in under 150 ms without reloading other workspaces' sleeping tabs, and every workspace is restored on the next launch; private browsing stays separate from all of them.

nodes.title: Import a sidebar's spaces and folders
nodes.promise: When the sidebar layout of a supported sidebar-tab browser is found on this Mac, import previews and recreates its spaces as workspaces with their pinned tabs, folders (nesting kept) and favourites; unsupported or unreadable files are reported, never half-imported.

nodes.title: Make a site yours
nodes.promise: From the site protection popover you can hide an element by pointing at it, choose a reading width, font and light or dark colours for that site, or add your own style rules; tweaks are stored only on this Mac, never run scripts, apply on every visit to that site (not to others), and can be turned off or removed per site.

nodes.title: Quick window for links from other apps
nodes.promise: With the setting on, a link opened from another app (Mail, Slack, Finder) shows in a small floating window with protection on; ⌘O moves it, with its history, into a tab of the main window (or a chosen workspace), closing it leaves no tab behind, and ⌥⌘N opens an empty one.

nodes.title: Video follows you
nodes.promise: With the setting on, switching away from a tab playing a video floats that video in picture-in-picture; returning to the tab docks it again; the sidebar shows a now-playing control that pauses, mutes or jumps to the tab; sites that refuse picture-in-picture keep playing in place.

nodes.title: Pages side by side
nodes.promise: Dragging a tab to the page's edge, or choosing Split with…, shows two tabs side by side with a draggable divider; each side navigates, finds and zooms on its own, the address bar and toolbar follow the focused side, the pair stays together in the tab list and on relaunch, and closing one side returns the other to full size.

nodes.title: Compare two outlets side by side
nodes.promise: From a world story's sources carousel, Compare opens two outlets' articles side by side, each labelled with its outlet and country, each side translatable on its own, and The Olds for that story one click away.
